incidente.resumo: A DDoS attack combining SYN flood, DNS reflection, ICMP flooding and NTP amplification (over 20Gbps) made Basecamp and the other services completely unavailable for 45 minutes and intermittent or slow for the rest of a 1 hour 40 minute window; network quarantine by other providers delayed full access until 11:08. Mitigation was filtering through a single provider and working with them to remove bogus traffic. No data was compromised.

descricao.texto: A DDoS attack on the network combining SYN flood, DNS reflection, ICMP flooding and NTP amplification, with a combined flow in excess of 20Gbps.
trechos: As we detailed in Basecamp was under network attack, criminals assaulted our network with a DDoS attack on March 24.
The attack was a combination of SYN flood, DNS reflection, ICMP flooding, and NTP amplification.
The combined flow was in excess of 20Gbps.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Basecamp was put in network quarantine by other providers, so access was not restored for everyone until 11:08, after the main attack ended around 10:12.
trechos: In addition to the attack itself, Basecamp got put in network quarantine by other providers, so it wasn’t until 11:08 that access was restored for everyone, everywhere.
The main attack lasted a total of an hour and 40 minutes starting at 8:32 central time and ending around 10:12.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The off-site status site received more traffic than ever before and also had availability problems.
trechos: Although we were successful at posting information to our status site (which is hosted off site), the site received more traffic than ever in the past, and it too had availability problems.

passos.texto: Traffic was filtered through a single provider, working with them to remove bogus traffic.
trechos: Our mitigation strategy included filtering through a single provider and working with them to remove bogus traffic.

acoes.texto: Already done: formed a DDoS Survivors group to collaborate with other sites subject to similar attacks.
trechos: We’ve formed a DDoS Survivors group to collaborate with other sites who’ve been subject to the same or similar attacks.

acoes.texto: Exploring vendor shields to mitigate future attacks faster, and initiating conversations with security vendors.
trechos: We’re exploring all sorts of vendor shields to be able to mitigate future attacks even faster.
We have discussed plans with our providers, and we’re initiating new conversations with some of the top security vendors.

acoes.texto: Already done: law enforcement was contacted and a statement added to their case file; the company will continue to assist them.
trechos: Law enforcement has been contacted, we’ve added our statement to their case file, and we’ll continue to assist them in catching the criminals behind this attack.

acoes.texto: Make changes so that reporting such an event to customers takes no more than 5 minutes.
trechos: We’ll make changes to ensure that it doesn’t take more than a maximum of 5 minutes to report something like this again.

acoes.texto: Already done: upgraded the servers that power the status site; additional load and availability testing is planned in the coming days.
trechos: We’ve already upgraded the servers that power the site and we’ll be conducting additional load and availability testing in the coming days.
The main attack lasted a total of an hour and 40 minutes starting at 8:32 central time and ending around 10:12.
In addition to the attack itself, Basecamp got put in network quarantine by other providers, so it wasn’t until 11:08 that access was restored for everyone, everywhere.

observacoes: The year 2014 comes from the comment/publication date written in the extracted text ('Mar 26 2014'), two days after the March 24 attack. The duration runs from the start of the attack (8:32) to full access at 11:08 (156 minutes); the attack itself lasted 1 hour 40 minutes, with 45 minutes of complete unavailability. The text states no data was compromised. Reader comments are included in the extracted text. categoria_causa follows the attack's mechanism: the DDoS flooded the network (over 20Gbps); there is no dedicated category for attacks. Communication: there was a 20-minute delay between first learning of the attack and reporting it to customers via Twitter and status.
